title: Clause width fold
statement: Let $C$ be a finite clause of literals, let $c\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ be a counter value, and let $g$ be a Boolean flag. Folding the width-pass transition over the binary encoding of $C$, starting in state $1$ with counter $c$ and flag $g$, ends in state $0$ with counter $0$ and flag $g\wedge[c+|C|\le 3]$, where $|C|$ counts literal occurrences, including repetitions.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a clause over natural-number-indexed variables
replaced:
Let $C$ be a clause, $c \in \{0,1,2,3\}$ a counter value, and $g$ a Boolean flag.
Folding the width-pass transition over the serialization of $C$, from the clause
position with counter $c$ and flag $g$, returns the formula position with counter
$0$ and flag $g \wedge [c + |C| \le 3]$, where $|C|$ counts literal occurrences
including repetitions.
